questions.prompt: What kind of bug is an integration test especially good at catching?

options.text: A typo inside one pure function
A mismatch at the seam between components (e.g., wrong column name or data format)

questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise real seams, catching bugs between correctly-built parts that unit tests mock away.

questions.prompt: What does it mean for an integration test to be 'hermetic'?

options.text: It is self-contained — brings its own data and depends on no shared or pre-existing state
It shares one database across all tests

questions.explanation: A hermetic test seeds its own data and doesn't depend on other tests or shared state, so it's repeatable and order-independent.

questions.prompt: A boundary where components connect — a database, HTTP client, or module interface — is called a ____.
questions.explanation: Integration tests target seams: the boundaries where separately-built parts meet.

questions.prompt: Which practices keep integration tests reliable? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use a fresh, disposable test database and seed exactly what's needed
Roll back each test's writes or clean up afterward
Point the tests at the shared production database
Fake third parties you don't own behind an adapter

questions.explanation: Disposable data, cleanup/rollback, and adapter-faking keep tests hermetic; using production is exactly what to avoid.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a database integration test using a fixture.

items.text: Create a fresh test database and schema
Run the code that writes and reads through it
Assert the resulting rows, then tear down

questions.explanation: Build a disposable DB, exercise the real seam, verify the outcome, and clean up.

questions.prompt: Match each boundary choice to when it's appropriate.

pairs.right: The integration with your own DB is what you're testing
Fast, realistic behavior without external setup
Rarely — prefer a fake adapter; a few smoke checks only

questions.explanation: Use real instances for what you own and are testing; fake or stub third parties and external services.
